rationale: A defensible consolidation of two economically distinct and independently strong archive legs (cash share of current assets and the dual-deflator cycle), and the expression matches the hypothesis, but it is an ensemble of already-tested components so the upside is incremental rather than a new mechanism.

This is a pure aggregator relabeling of the already-tested CashConversionCycleInDays leg (rank-sum instead of difference of the same two duration ratios), i.e. exactly the kind of cosmetic functional-form variant the objective warns against, and it also loses the economically meaningful "days-in minus days-out" interpretation that motivated the parent.

Strengthening the profitability leg with operating cash flow is a genuinely untested axis here and internally consistent, but the gross-profit-plus-OCF composite is close to published cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016) and oancf will cut sample depth, so novelty and coverage both need to be checked.

This is the classic Sloan earnings-minus-cash accrual anomaly interacted with gross profitability — a construct already run several times in this archive — with only a deflator swap, and the claim that (act − che) is "well behaved" is wrong for the many firms with tiny non-cash current assets, where the unwinsorized ratio will explode and drive the extreme portfolio buckets.

Substituting oibdp for gross profit in the existing CashConversionCycleInDays signal is a single-leg ablation rather than a new signal, and the analogous test on the flow family (OperatingProfitXSupplierCredit) already answered the same question, so the expected information gain is diagnostic and small.

Two of the three "complementary" channels (net working capital per sales and the operating-liability share of the cycle) are near-algebraic restatements of the same working-capital block, making this a redundant kitchen-sink stack, and the nested SUMRANK silently assigns the cash-share channel half the weight, contradicting the stated equal-channel rationale.
